name: Rhode Island

agency.name: Rhode Island Department of Labor and Training, Labor Standards Unit

rates2027.note: set by statute (RIGL 28-12-3), listed on the DLT minimum wage page

tipped.note: Maximum tip credit $12.11; cash wage plus tips must reach $16.00.

minWage.other: Full-time students under 19 at nonprofit/religious/library/community organizations: 90% ($14.40); 14-15-year-olds working 24 h/week or less: 75% ($12.00).

source.quote: Commencing January 1, 2027: $17.00 per hour * Commencing January 1, 2026: $16.00 per hour

overtime.note: Separate rule: time and one-half for work on Sundays and holidays (with exceptions); retail Sunday/holiday premium hours are excluded from weekly overtime.

source.quote: If you work more than 40 hours in a week, you must be paid one and one-half times your regular rate of pay for any additional hours worked after the standard 40 hours.

sickLeave.capNote: Up to 40 hours per year; paid at employers with 18+ employees, unpaid but protected at 17 or fewer.
sickLeave.note: Healthy and Safe Families and Workplaces Act (RIGL 28-57).

source.quote: they are entitled to earn at least one hour of sick/safe leave for every 35 hours worked ... Full-time employees may earn and use up to 40 hours per year.

familyLeave.name: Rhode Island Temporary Caregiver Insurance (TCI)
familyLeave.replacement: Weekly benefit rate based on base-period wages; minimum $148, plus a dependency allowance (greater of $20 or 7% of the rate per dependent, up to 5)
familyLeave.medicalLeave: Temporary Disability Insurance (TDI): up to 30 weeks for the worker's own non-work illness or injury (TCI weeks reduce TDI weeks).
familyLeave.stateUnpaidLaw: RI Parental and Family Medical Leave Act: 13 consecutive weeks of unpaid job-protected leave (employers with 50+ employees, 12 months of service).

source.quote: For claims with a Benefit Year beginning date of 7/1/26 or later, $1,150.00 is the maximum benefit rate, and the minimum benefit rate is $148.

finalPay.fired: by the next regular payday (within 24 hours if the business is liquidated, merged, sold or moved out of state)
finalPay.ptoNote: Accrued vacation must be paid at separation once the employee has completed at least 1 year of service.

source.quote: Whenever an employee is separated from the payroll, the unpaid wages or compensation of such employee shall become due on the next regular payday

ptoSource.quote: they are required to pay out any remaining accrued vacation pay upon separation if you work for them for at least one year.

breaks.meal: 20-minute mealtime for a 6-hour shift, 30 minutes for an 8-hour shift (unpaid); not required in licensed health care facilities or where fewer than 3 employees are on site

source.quote: Employees must be given a twenty-minute mealtime for a six-hour shift, and a thirty-minute mealtime for an eight-hour shift.

notes.text: Rhode Island requires time-and-a-half for work on Sundays and holidays in most businesses, on top of weekly overtime rules.

source.quote: Employees must be paid at least one and one-half times your normal rate of pay for any work performed on Sundays and holidays.

notes.text: Since January 1, 2026, bone marrow donors can use one week of TCI and organ donors thirty business days.

source.quote: Effective 1/1/26: bone marrow donors can access one week of TCI, and organ donors can access thirty business days of TCI.

notes.text: Minimum wage rises to $17.00 on January 1, 2027.

uncertain: dlt.ri.gov blocks curl and WebFetch (HTTP 403); all DLT pages and PDFs were read through a text-rendering proxy (r.jina.ai). Quotes are verbatim from the official pages.
TCI date benefits first became payable not stated on pages read (left null; program enacted July 11, 2013 per DLT).

TCI weekly benefit formula (share of high-quarter wages) not stated on pages read; maximum $1,150 applies to benefit years beginning on or after 2026-07-01 (earlier 2026 claims had a lower cap, not verified).
